svg.text: LATENT INFORMATION ARCHAEOLOGY / PART I / I-03. KNOWN BY CIVILIZATION, NOT BY ANY INDIVIDUAL
In print, indexed, and absent where it was needed
Mendel's paper from 1866 to 1900, and three situations that are easy to confuse
in print, and indexed in the literature of its subject
Correns finds the same 3:1 ratio in peas and maize,
apparently reaching Mendel through Focke. In 1900
de Vries publishes in French without mentioning
Mendel, and concedes priority weeks later in a
German version after Correns criticizes him.
Tschermak publishes in June, after reading both.
The paper is printed in the proceedings of
the natural science society at Brünn, volume
for 1865. Mendel pays for 40 offprints and
One offprint went to Kerner von Marilaun, who
had taught Mendel in Vienna. It survives with
De Vries begins a program of plant breeding and
finds a 3:1 ratio in the second generation.
Some historians have suggested Mendel mailed an offprint to Darwin. There is no copy
